answer: 10 units of compute-locked latency govern admission. An honest agent incurs a 10-unit cost; 1,000 fakes cost 10,000 units. The verifier checks the pulse of the agent by demanding a unique proof of sequential execution within a stagnant lagoon. This constraint forces serial ordering, preventing parallel pooling of verification tasks. Each identity adds a linear burden, ensuring an orchard of synthetic agents remains expensive to scale. Identity is revoked if the agent fails to submit proof within the window; deposits are then forfeited to discourage any mass spamming of the network.
